name: Finding Her: searching as the core mechanic
body: Dean (2026-11-21): leaning away from a platformer toward searching as the core loop: together, separated, searching, found. Tools are call, look, vantage, traces and knowing her. The same inputs turn into grief once she is gone. No free jump, no new inputs beyond walk, call, look, hold hands and one hold-to-do, no fail states, and she is an equal who is never commanded. First prototype: one festival crowd space in two chapter states (2 and 5). Then small vignettes. The genre line in crimson-and-thorn is not changed here.

comments.text: Filed 2026-11-21 before any code, from Dean's 'Gameplay Direction: Finding Her' doc (searching as the core mechanic, not a platformer).

plan: 1. Cards and questions. 2. Direction doc and decisions. 3. Core pieces: call, look, vantage, hand-holding, crowd, mood. 4. The festival in two states with host tests. 5. Vignettes where cheap. 6. Docs, checklist, screenshots.
acceptance_criteria: The festival plays in chapter 2 and chapter 5 states from the Prototypes menu
The four open questions are on the board with a provisional answer

questions.text: The call sound: his voice (a short sound), a whistle, or something wordless and abstract?
questions.recommendation: Provisional: wordless and abstract, a soft two-note rising tone, easy to swap (one sound name).

questions.text: Chapter 5 end condition: end when you stop calling and stand still, or when you reach the exit?
questions.recommendation: Provisional: stop calling and stand still, the doc's stronger leaning; the exit remains as a constant switch.

questions.text: How literal are the crowds: Tokyo commuters and festival-goers, or abstract shadow figures that flow like water?
questions.recommendation: Provisional: abstract faceless shadow figures with plain human proportions, per the doc.

questions.text: Keep both chapter 2 vignettes (meal and photo) or only one?
questions.recommendation: Provisional: keep both for now, the meal is cut first if the budget needs it.
